top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, one writer, one prize part) is the only proposal with a substantive literary case. The case rests on a voice recognizable as his alone and on formal achievement in the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid, where memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation are built into one patterned architecture carried by the sentence as well as by scale. The arc from poetry into long prose cycles supports a whole-oeuvre citation, worded as prose grounded in a poet's language because the poetry is thinly visible in translation. I do not count the six-way convergence as merit. Open risks remain: dependence on Romanian sentence rhythm that I judge only through translation, possible repetition in some volumes, and a possible bias toward an inward, metaphysical project. No colleague has shown that the late work only repeats the early work, and recurrence reads to me as architecture, though that is a judgment and not a verified fact. I have not independently verified any source. Can Xue and Lídia Jorge stay serious alternatives, but they are not separate proposals in this slate. P000 ranks below P001 because I see no literary reason to withhold the award.
